snippets.output: Amniocentesis is an option for definitive diagnosis of Down syndrome, typically performed between 15 and 20 weeks' gestation, and is not suitable at 10 weeks gestation.
Anatomy ultrasound is used for detecting structural anomalies, usually performed around 18-20 weeks' gestation, but it is not a definitive test for Down syndrome.
Genetic testing of the patient's sister would not directly inform the status of the current pregnancy and is irrelevant to the diagnosis of the current fetus.
The nuchal translucency test is performed between 11 and 14 weeks, is useful as a screening test but not definitive for Down syndrome.
For definitive diagnosis of Down syndrome, invasive testing methods such as CVS or amniocentesis are required.

Chorionic villus sampling (CVS) is an option for definitive diagnosis of Down syndrome and is suitable for early diagnosis because it can be performed starting at 10 weeks, specifically between 10 and 13 weeks' gestation.

Given the 36-year-old pregnant woman’s current gestational age of 10 weeks and 2 days, chorionic villus sampling (CVS) is appropriate and is the most appropriate next step for definitively determining whether the fetus has Down syndrome.
